sources.entry: Weechat - Fast, light and extensible chat client. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C/Docker/deb

summary.one_liner: WeeChat is a fast, lightweight, extensible terminal chat client, best known for IRC, with a modular core and scripting support.
summary.what_it_does: WeeChat is a chat client built around a small core with optional plugins, and the IRC plugin is one of them. The README says the IRC plugin follows RFCs 1459, 2810, 2811, 2812, 2813 and 7194. It can be extended with C plugins and scripts in Perl, Python, Ruby, Lua, Tcl, Scheme, JavaScript and PHP. A headless mode (weechat-headless) lets it run in the background, and the relay plugin lets remote interfaces connect to it or use it as an IRC proxy. The /upgrade command reloads the binary in place while keeping buffers and server connections. The README lists GNU/Linux, BSD, GNU/Hurd, Haiku, macOS and Windows (via WSL or Cygwin) as supported platforms.
use_cases: Chatting on IRC from a terminal
Running a persistent IRC client on a server
Remote access to a chat session
Connecting to multiple chat networks from one client
notable: Modular core where IRC and other protocols are independent, unloadable plugins
Upgrade in place with /upgrade, keeping connections and buffer contents
Headless mode plus relay plugin for remote access or acting as an IRC proxy
Scripting in many languages including Python, Perl, Lua and Ruby
caveats: Only the latest stable version is supported, per the README's SECURITY.md reference
Full feature set depends on optional dependencies and CMake options, so some builds need more setup
